record.paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
record.original_question: For weak solutions of the initial-boundary value problem for the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18), can one prove uniqueness in dimensions n ≥ 2 without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?

evidence.quote: К первой группе относятся проблема сильной глобальной разрешимости начально-краевой задачи, проблема регулярности слабых решений, проблема единственности слабых решений, оценка хаусдорфовой размерности траекторных и глобальных аттракторов3 (все эти задачи требуют решения без ограничений на коэффициенты, внешнюю силу и начальные данные).
Важно, что для Навье-Стокса эти задачи актуальны при n ≥ 3, а для (0.2),(0.4),(0.5),(2.18) — при n ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $T>0$. Consider the initial–boundary value problem for the motion of an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys type:
$$
\partial_t v+(v\cdot\nabla)v=-\nabla p+\operatorname{Div}\sigma+f\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
$$
$$
\operatorname{div} v=0\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),
$$
together with the rheological (constitutive) relation of Jeffreys type
$$
\sigma+\lambda_1\bigl(\partial_t\sigma+(v\cdot\nabla)\sigma+\sigma W(v)-W(v)\sigma\bigr)=2\eta\bigl(\mathcal{E}(v)+\lambda_2(\partial_t\mathcal{E}(v)+(v\cdot\nabla)\mathcal{E}(v)+\mathcal{E}(v)W(v)-W(v)\mathcal{E}(v))\bigr),
$$
where $\mathcal{E}(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v+\nabla v^{\top})$, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v-\nabla v^{\top})$, $\eta>0$, and $0<\lambda_2<\lambda_1$ are constants. Impose the no-slip condition
$$
v|_{\partial\Omega\times(0,T)}=0,
$$
and the initial conditions
$$
v|_{t=0}=v_0\in L^2_{\mathrm{div}}(\Omega),\qquad \sigma|_{t=0}=\sigma_0,
$$
with external force $f\in L^2(0,T;H^{-1}(\Omega))$. A weak solution is a pair $(v,\sigma)$ in the natural energy class satisfying the system in the standard distributional/integral sense.

Question: For all dimensions $n\ge 2$, can one establish uniqueness of weak solutions of this initial–boundary value problem without imposing any additional smallness or smoothness restrictions on the coefficients $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\eta$, the external force $f$, or the initial data $(v_0,\sigma_0)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on Jeffreys-type viscoelastic models (Vorotnikov–Zvyagin and follow-ups) establishes existence of weak solutions, regularization, and attractor results, but unconditional uniqueness of weak solutions in dimensions $n\ge 2$ without restrictions on coefficients, force, or data is not reported as resolved. Like the analogous Navier–Stokes uniqueness problem (open for $n\ge 3$), this remains a listed open problem for the Jeffreys system in $n\ge 2$.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of weak solutions for the initial-boundary value problem in the Jeffreys model
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of weak solutions established in 2D/3D bounded domains; uniqueness not asserted unconditionally.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known but unconditional uniqueness of weak solutions is not established in this framework.

status_evidence.title: Trajectory and Global Attractors for Jeffreys viscoelastic medium
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs minimal trajectory and global attractors because uniqueness of weak solutions is unavailable.
status_evidence.claim: The use of trajectory attractors indicates uniqueness of weak solutions remains open.

status_evidence.title: Dmitry Vorotnikov publications
status_evidence.snippet: List of works on Jeffreys-type models including energy inequality and partial uniqueness results.
status_evidence.claim: No paper claims unconditional uniqueness of weak solutions for $n\ge 2$.
